complexity.notes: The local name `dict` shadows the builtin — use another name. The counting and second pass are redundant: a single loop that returns True the moment a value is already in the collection (a set suffices, no counts needed) does the same job in one pass with early exit, and typically returns False faster on duplicate-free inputs too.
complexity.summary: Counts every value in a dict, then makes a second pass over nums returning True at the first count above 1.
